key_insight: Scaling U-Net width and depth enables accurate prediction of full 36-component strain localization tensor fields in 3D concrete microstructures, while conventional channel doubling is suboptimal.
engineering_relevance: The surrogate could accelerate repeated mechanical-field evaluations in computational homogenization and multiscale simulations.
method: Train a U-Net on voxelized concrete mesostructures using localization tensors from an FFT-based linear elastic solver.
Optimize architecture and scaling for resolutions up to 256³, balancing accuracy and inference speed.
Use Maximum Mean Discrepancy on internal feature maps to flag out-of-distribution microstructures.
evidence_signal: The final network reports 1.118% Mean Absolute Error on both validation and held-out test sets, with approximately 8.7× faster inference than the FFT solver on an Nvidia H100 GPU.
watch_item: Generalization depends on training morphology diversity; transfer to unfamiliar microstructures requires caution and out-of-distribution screening.
paper_title: Neural network scaling and generalization for 3D strain fields in heterogeneous materials
